sections.md:
### Information System registration

The EUDR Information System must provide "registration of operators and traders and their authorised representatives in the Union; for operators placing relevant products under the customs procedure 'release for free circulation' or 'export', the Economic Operators Registration and Identification (EORI) number established pursuant to Article 9 of Regulation (EU) No 952/2013, shall be included in their registration profile." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 33(2)(a), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

*Operational implication:* Workspaces that import or export relevant products for free circulation must have their EORI number linked to their Information System registration. This is a precondition for submitting due diligence statements.

Under Regulation 2025/2650: "Downstream operators and traders 'other than SMEs' will not have to file returns but will need to register in the Information System." *Source: European Commission Access2Markets, "Delay until December 2026," European Commission, 28 January 2026. https://trade.ec.europa.eu/access-to-markets/en/news/delay-until-december-2026-and-other-developments-implementation-eudr-regulation

### Annual public reporting (non-SME operators, Article 12(3))

"Operators who do not fall within the categories of SMEs, including microenterprises, or natural persons shall, on an annual basis, publicly report as widely as possible, including via the internet, on their due diligence system, including on the steps taken by them to fulfil their obligations as set out in Article 8." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 12(3), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

The report must include: a summary of the Article 9(1)(a)–(c) information (description, quantity, country of production); conclusions of the risk assessment and mitigation measures; and "where applicable, a description of the process of consultation of indigenous peoples, local communities and other customary tenure rights holders or of the civil society organisations that are present in the area of production." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 12(4), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

"Operators who fall also within the scope of other Union legal acts that lay down requirements regarding value chain due diligence may fulfil their reporting obligations under this paragraph by including the required information when reporting in the context of those other Union legal acts." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 12(3), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115 *Operational implication:* Workspaces already reporting under CSRD or CSDDD may be able to consolidate EUDR reporting into those existing frameworks, reducing duplication.

### Member State competent authority reporting

Member States must designate competent authorities by 30 December 2023. *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 14(2), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115 The Commission publishes the list of designated competent authorities. *Source: European Commission DG Environment, "Regulation on Deforestation-free Products," European Commission. https://environment.ec.europa.eu/topics/forests/deforestation/regulation-deforestation-free-products_en

### Customs reference number requirement

"The reference number of the due diligence statement shall be made available to customs authorities before the release for free circulation or export of a relevant product entering or leaving the market." Except where the due diligence statement is made available through the electronic interface referred to in Article 28(2), "the person lodging the customs declaration for release for free circulation or export of a relevant product shall make available to customs authorities the reference number of the due diligence statement assigned to that relevant product by the information system." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 26(4), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

*Operational implication:* For workspaces lodging customs declarations (as customs broker or importer of record) for relevant products, having the DDS reference number available at the time of customs declaration submission is a procedural prerequisite.

### Record retention periods

- Due diligence statements: five years from the date of submission. *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 4(3), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115
- Article 9 information: five years from the date of placing on the market or export. *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 9(1), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115
- Due diligence documentation (measures and procedures): at least five years. *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 12(5), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115
- SME trader records: at least five years. *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 5(4), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115
- Competent authority check records: at least 10 years. *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 16(14), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

**What the EUDR is:**

The EUDR establishes rules regarding the placing and making available on the Union market and the export from the Union of relevant products that contain, have been fed with, or have been made using relevant commodities. The regulation's stated purposes are: "(a) minimising the Union's contribution to deforestation and forest degradation worldwide, and thereby contributing to a reduction in global deforestation; (b) reducing the Union's contribution to greenhouse gas emissions and global biodiversity loss." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 1(1), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

The seven covered commodities, as defined in Article 2(1), are: "cattle, cocoa, coffee, oil palm, rubber, soya and wood." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 2(1), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

"Relevant products" are defined as "products listed in Annex I that contain, have been fed with or have been made using relevant commodities." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 2(2), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115 These include, per Annex I: leather and cattle hides, chocolate and cocoa products, coffee, palm oil derivatives, rubber products (tyres, gloves, tubes), soya products, and a broad range of wood and wood-derived products including furniture, paper and pulp, printed books, and prefabricated wooden buildings.

**Effective date slot:** The regulation entered into force on "the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union," i.e., 29 June 2023. *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 38(1), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

**Jurisdictional scope slot:** The regulation applies to relevant commodities and relevant products "produced within the Union as well as commodities and products imported to the Union," as stated in recital 23. *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Recital 23, European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115 It is "binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Final clause, European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

**Why it applies to freight and logistics workspaces:**

The regulation's operator definition reaches any entity that first places covered products on the EU market. Article 7 states: "Where a natural or legal person established outside the Union places relevant products on the market, the first natural or legal person established in the Union who makes such relevant products available on the market shall be deemed to be an operator within the meaning of this Regulation." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 7, European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether a workspace acting as freight forwarder, customs agent, importer of record, or logistics provider qualifies as an "operator" (who first places products on the market) or a "trader" (any other supply-chain person who makes products available on the market), and whether those roles trigger due diligence obligations or lighter collection-and-record obligations, requires legal counsel review mapped to the workspace's precise commercial arrangements per transaction type.

Article 30 of the EUDR also states "operators and traders should be bound by the obligations under this Regulation regardless of whether the making available on the market takes place through traditional or online means." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Recital 30, European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

Additionally: "the Commission and the Member States should monitor the implementation of this Regulation and identify whether digital and technological developments require further specifications or initiatives, as appropriate, in the future." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Recital 30, European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

### 1 — Products produced before 29 June 2023

Regulation does "not apply to relevant products listed in Annex I produced before the date indicated in Article 38(1)" (29 June 2023), with the exception of timber/timber products produced before 29 June 2023 placed on the market from 31 December 2027 (Article 37(3) carve-out). *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Articles 1(2) and 37(2)–(3), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

### 2 — Recycled/end-of-lifecycle products

Products "produced entirely from material that has completed its lifecycle and would otherwise have been discarded as waste as defined in Article 3, point (1), of Directive 2008/98/EC" are excluded. This exclusion does "not apply to certain by-products of the manufacturing process." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Annex I preamble, European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

### 3 — Private use by EU consumers

*Analytical inference:* The updated FAQs confirm that EU consumers purchasing for private use are not operators. *Source: Latham & Watkins / Global ELR, "European Commission Releases New EU Deforestation Regulation Measures," Global ELR, 7 May 2026. https://www.globalelr.com/2026/05/european-commission-releases-new-eu-deforestation-regulation-measures The regulation defines "in the course of a commercial activity" as "for the purpose of processing, for distribution to commercial or non-commercial consumers, or for use in the business of the operator or trader itself." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 2(19), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

### 4 — FLEGT-licensed wood products

"Wood products which fall within the scope of Regulation (EC) No 2173/2005 that are covered by a valid FLEGT license from an operational licensing scheme shall be deemed to comply with Article 3, point (b)" (the legality requirement) only. The deforestation-free requirement (Article 3(a)) and the due diligence statement requirement (Article 3(c)) remain in force. *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 10(3), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

### 5 — SME operator derogation for already-subject-to-due-diligence products

SME operators are not required to exercise full due diligence (Articles 10–11) for relevant products that have already been subject to due diligence and for which a due diligence statement has been submitted. They provide the reference number upon request. The derogation applies only to the already-covered portion; parts not subject to prior due diligence require full due diligence. *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 4(8), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

### 6 — Authorised representative delegation

"Operators or traders may mandate an authorised representative to submit the due diligence statement … on their behalf. In such cases, the operator or trader shall retain responsibility for the compliance of the relevant product with Article 3." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 6(1), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115 Additionally: "An operator that is a natural person or a microenterprise may mandate the next operator or trader further down the supply chain that is not a natural person or a microenterprise to act as an authorised representative." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 6(3), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

### 7 — Proposed exemptions under draft delegated act (not yet in force)

The draft delegated act open for consultation until 1 June 2026 proposes horizontal exemptions for: samples and products used for examination, analysis, and testing; single-use and reusable packaging materials and containers; marketing and information materials; waste, used, and secondhand products; and items of correspondence. *Source: Latham & Watkins / Global ELR, "European Commission Releases New EU Deforestation Regulation Measures," Global ELR, 7 May 2026. https://www.globalelr.com/2026/05/european-commission-releases-new-eu-deforestation-regulation-measures These are proposed, not yet in force. Monitor Commission adoption.

### 8 — Bamboo-based paper products

Per Annex I, pulp and paper of Chapters 47 and 48 are in scope "with the exception of bamboo-based and recovered (waste and scrap) products." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Annex I, European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

### Q1: Does this regulation apply to products produced before 29 June 2023?

**Decided (by the text):** Article 1(2) states: "Except as provided for in Article 37(3), this Regulation does not apply to relevant products listed in Annex I produced before the date indicated in Article 38(1)," i.e., before 29 June 2023. *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 1(2), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115 Article 37(3) creates a carve-out: timber and timber products produced before 29 June 2023 and placed on the market from 31 December 2027 shall comply with Article 3 of the new regulation. *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 37(3), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

### Q2: What is the operative cut-off date for "deforestation-free"?

**Decided (by the text):** "Deforestation-free" means the relevant products contain or have been made using relevant commodities "that were produced on land that has not been subject to deforestation after 31 December, 2020" and, for wood products, that "the wood has been harvested from the forest without inducing forest degradation after 31 December, 2020." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 2(13), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

### Q3: Is "forest" defined in the regulation?

**Decided (by the text):** The regulation defines "forest" as "land spanning more than 0,5 hectares with trees higher than 5 metres and a canopy cover of more than 10 %, or trees able to reach those thresholds in situ, excluding land that is predominantly under agricultural or urban land use." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 2(4), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115 This largely follows FAO definitions. *Source: World Resources Institute, "What Is the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR)?", WRI, 15 May 2026. https://www.wri.org/insights/explain-eu-deforestation-regulation

### Q4: Do SME traders face the same obligations as operators?

**Decided (by the text, with qualification):** SME traders must collect and retain reference numbers and contact data, but they do not submit due diligence statements. Non-SME traders carry the same obligations as operators. The distinction between SME and non-SME turns on the definition in "Article 3 of Directive 2013/34/EU." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 5, Article 2(30), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115 *Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether the workspace qualifies as an SME under Directive 2013/34/EU (the EU Accounting Directive's headcount/turnover/balance sheet thresholds) requires legal and financial assessment.

### Q5: Does the regulation apply to agroforestry, plantations, and managed forests?

**Decided (by the text):** "Agroforestry systems, including where crops are grown under tree cover, as well as agrisilvicultural, silvopastoral and agrosilvopastoral systems, should not be considered forests, but as constituting agricultural use." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Recital 37, European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115 Plantation forests (intensively managed, single or two species, even age class, regular spacing) are defined separately from primary forests; the deforestation definition specifically covers conversion to agricultural use. *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 2(11), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

### Q6: Does the regulation apply to recycled products?

**Decided (by the text, with qualification):** Products produced entirely from material that has completed its lifecycle and would otherwise be discarded as waste (per Directive 2008/98/EC Article 3(1)) are excluded. However, "this should not apply to certain by-products of the manufacturing process." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Recital 40 and Annex I preamble, European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

### Q7: Does FLEGT licensing satisfy the legality requirement?

**Decided (by the text):** "Wood products which fall within the scope of Regulation (EC) No 2173/2005 that are covered by a valid FLEGT license from an operational licensing scheme shall be deemed to comply with Article 3, point (b), of this Regulation." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 10(3), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115 FLEGT licenses do not substitute for the deforestation-free requirement (Article 3(a)); they address only legality (Article 3(b)).

The EUDR creates distinct obligation tiers based on defined role categories. As enacted and subsequently amended by Regulation 2025/2650:

**Operator (as defined in the original regulation):** "any natural or legal person who, in the course of a commercial activity, places relevant products on the market or exports them." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 2(15), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

**Downstream operator (new category under Regulation 2025/2650):** "a natural or legal person who, in the course of a commercial activity, places on the market or exports regulated products made from regulated materials, all of which are covered by a due diligence declaration or a simplified declaration." Processors and exporters can be considered downstream operators depending on their role. *Source: European Commission Access2Markets, "Delay until December 2026," European Commission, 28 January 2026. https://trade.ec.europa.eu/access-to-markets/en/news/delay-until-december-2026-and-other-developments-implementation-eudr-regulation

**Micro or small primary operator (new category under Regulation 2025/2650):** "a natural person or micro or small enterprise, under EU accounting rules, established in a low-risk country which places on the market or exports the regulated products they themselves have grown or obtained." *Source: European Commission Access2Markets, "Delay until December 2026," European Commission, 28 January 2026. https://trade.ec.europa.eu/access-to-markets/en/news/delay-until-december-2026-and-other-developments-implementation-eudr-regulation

**Trader:** "any person in the supply chain other than the operator who, in the course of a commercial activity, makes relevant products available on the market." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 2(17), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

**Non-SME traders** are treated as non-SME operators and carry the same due diligence obligations. *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 5(1), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

**SME traders** collect and keep: name, postal address, email address of suppliers and downstream traders, and the reference numbers of due diligence statements associated with those products; they retain this information for at least five years. *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 5(3) and (4), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

**Article 7 (placing on the market by operators established in third countries):** "Where a natural or legal person established outside the Union places relevant products on the market, the first natural or legal person established in the Union who makes such relevant products available on the market shall be deemed to be an operator within the meaning of this Regulation." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 7, European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether the workspace, depending on its commercial role in a given transaction (importer of record, freight forwarder, customs broker, or distribution hub operator), meets the defined terms "operator," "downstream operator," "trader," or "SME trader" is a legal determination requiring counsel review. The answer will differ across the workspace's transaction types and cargo verticals.

**Obligation comparison by role:**

| Role | DDS submission | Geolocation required | Risk assessment | Annual reporting |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Operator (primary) | Yes — submit own DDS | Yes | Yes (Articles 10–11) | Yes (non-SMEs, Article 12(3)) |
| Downstream operator | No — collect/retain reference number only | No (use upstream DDS) | Verification only | Registration in IS required |
| Non-SME trader | Same as operator | Yes (via due diligence) | Yes | Yes |
| SME trader | No — collect/retain reference number + contact data | No | No | No |

*Source for obligation structure: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Articles 4, 5, 12, European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115; corroborated by European Commission Access2Markets, 28 January 2026. https://trade.ec.europa.eu/access-to-markets/en/news/delay-until-december-2026-and-other-developments-implementation-eudr-regulation

The Commission has published official guidance documents and FAQs to support implementation. As of the May 2026 simplification package, the Commission released the third edition of its guidance document and the fifth iteration of its FAQ. *Source: Latham & Watkins / Global ELR, "European Commission Releases New EU Deforestation Regulation Measures," Global ELR, 7 May 2026. https://www.globalelr.com/2026/05/european-commission-releases-new-eu-deforestation-regulation-measures

**Key guidance provisions relevant to freight/logistics workspaces:**

**Product scope clarifications (FAQ Chapter 2, May 2026):** The May 2026 FAQs provide "further clarity on which products, activities, and situations fall within the EUDR's remit. Key updates include revised guidance on the treatment of wood and paper used for packaging, recycled paper and paperboard, tyres, and products listed in Annex I that do not themselves contain listed commodities (such as bamboo)." *Source: Latham & Watkins / Global ELR, "European Commission Releases New EU Deforestation Regulation Measures," Global ELR, 7 May 2026. https://www.globalelr.com/2026/05/european-commission-releases-new-eu-deforestation-regulation-measures

**Online and distance sales:** The updated FAQs "confirmed [EU] consumers purchasing for private use [are] not operators." *Source: Latham & Watkins / Global ELR, "European Commission Releases New EU Deforestation Regulation Measures," Global ELR, 7 May 2026. https://www.globalelr.com/2026/05/european-commission-releases-new-eu-deforestation-regulation-measures

**Re-imports:** The guidance "clarifies the treatment of re-imports as a downstream activity with use of a conventional reference number at customs." *Source: Latham & Watkins / Global ELR, "European Commission Releases New EU Deforestation Regulation Measures," Global ELR, 7 May 2026. https://www.globalelr.com/2026/05/european-commission-releases-new-eu-deforestation-regulation-measures

**Dual roles:** The guidance clarifies "dual roles within a single supply chain." *Source: Latham & Watkins / Global ELR, "European Commission Releases New EU Deforestation Regulation Measures," Global ELR, 7 May 2026. https://www.globalelr.com/2026/05/european-commission-releases-new-eu-deforestation-regulation-measures *Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether the workspace holds dual roles in specific transactions (e.g., acting simultaneously as freight forwarder and importer of record) and the compliance consequences of those dual roles require counsel review with reference to the Commission's guidance.

**Downstream obligation (FAQ Chapters 3 and 5):** New FAQs clarify "the obligation of first downstream operators to collect reference numbers from upstream operators is passive (with no duty to proactively investigate the veracity of such information)." *Source: Latham & Watkins / Global ELR, "European Commission Releases New EU Deforestation Regulation Measures," Global ELR, 7 May 2026. https://www.globalelr.com/2026/05/european-commission-releases-new-eu-deforestation-regulation-measures

**EUDR and other EU due diligence laws:** The guidance clarifies "the use of EUDR due diligence systems for other EU due diligence-related laws, subject to those instruments' additional requirements." *Source: Latham & Watkins / Global ELR, "European Commission Releases New EU Deforestation Regulation Measures," Global ELR, 7 May 2026. https://www.globalelr.com/2026/05/european-commission-releases-new-eu-deforestation-regulation-measures

**Geolocation conversion:** Article 15(1) notes that technical assistance "shall take into account the situation of SMEs, including microenterprises, and natural persons, in order to facilitate compliance with this Regulation, including as regards the conversion of data from relevant systems to identify the geolocation in the information system as referred to in Article 33." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 15(1), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

**Recycled/waste products:** Regulation (EU) 2023/1115 does not apply to goods "if they are produced entirely from material that has completed its lifecycle and would otherwise have been discarded as waste as defined in Article 3, point (1), of Directive 2008/98/EC." This exclusion does "not apply to certain by-products of the manufacturing process." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Annex I preamble, European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

**Compliance cost reduction estimate:** The Commission's May 2026 simplification review "estimates that the simplification measures will reduce annual compliance costs for companies subject to EUDR obligations by 75%." *Source: Latham & Watkins / Global ELR, "European Commission Releases New EU Deforestation Regulation Measures," Global ELR, 7 May 2026. https://www.globalelr.com/2026/05/european-commission-releases-new-eu-deforestation-regulation-measures *Analytical inference:* This estimate applies to the overall industry average, not to specific workspace types; high-volume importers of complex mixed-commodity products may see proportionally lower savings than simple downstream traders.

This brief covers Regulation (EU) 2023/1115 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 31 May 2023 on the making available on the Union market and the export from the Union of certain commodities and products associated with deforestation and forest degradation (EUDR), as subsequently amended by Regulation (EU) 2025/2650. It addresses the regulation's substantive requirements, compliance deadlines, supply-chain role placement, and operational implications for workspaces operating as freight forwarders, importers, exporters, and supply-chain intermediaries across air, road, and ocean transport modes, with cargo verticals spanning high-value goods, time-sensitive commodities, and manufactured products.

**Convention notes:**
- "FACT" labels mark verbatim-span-grounded claims.
- "Analytical inference:", "Industry interpretation:", and "Operational implication:" labels mark all analytical, interpretive, or forward-looking claims.
- "*Legal Confirmation Required:*" routes all conclusions about whether the workspace meets a defined regulatory role.
- All source URLs are drawn exclusively from the corpus SOURCE blocks or the New Sources Identified table.
- Effective date: 29 June 2023. Primary compliance deadline for large/medium operators: 30 December 2026 (amended). See Section 14 for the full timeline.

### 1 — WINDOW CLOSING: Map cargo flows against the EUDR's Annex I product list

**Action:** Map all commodities and products currently handled, forwarded, imported, or exported by the workspace against the EUDR's Annex I product list and CN codes within 30 days.

*Operational implication:* The Annex I scope is broad. Wood products covered extend from raw logs (CN 4403) through pulp, paper (Chapters 47–48), furniture (CN 9403), and prefabricated wooden buildings (CN 9406 10). Cattle-derived products include fresh/frozen meat (ex 0201, ex 0202), leather (ex 4101, ex 4104, ex 4107), and other prepared meats (ex 1602 50). Rubber covers tyres (ex 4011), gloves (ex 4015), and conveyor belts (ex 4010). Any workspace handling these across EU-import or EU-export flows may be exposed to compliance obligations that attach to whoever first places them on the EU market. *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Annex I, European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

### 2 — ACTION REQUIRED: Determine supply-chain role per transaction type before 30 December 2026

**Action:** Engage legal counsel to determine, for each transaction type, whether the workspace qualifies as an "operator," a "downstream operator" (new category introduced by Regulation 2025/2650), a "trader," or an "SME trader," since obligations differ materially by role.

*Operational implication:* Under Regulation 2025/2650, the obligation and responsibility to submit a due diligence statement lies exclusively with the operators who first place the product on the market. Operators and traders downstream in the supply chain no longer have to submit their own due diligence statements; they must instead collect and retain the reference number of the initial declaration made by the primary operator. *Source: European Commission Access2Markets, "Delay until December 2026 and other developments in the implementation of the EUDR Regulation," European Commission, 28 January 2026. https://trade.ec.europa.eu/access-to-markets/en/news/delay-until-december-2026-and-other-developments-implementation-eudr-regulation

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether any specific transaction structure (e.g., acting as importer of record for a non-EU client, or receiving goods from a non-EU producer and placing them on the EU market for the first time) attaches operator obligations requires counsel review.

### 3 — ACTION REQUIRED: Register in the EUDR Information System before 30 December 2026

**Action:** Register the workspace (and any authorised representatives) in the Commission's EUDR Information System, which was launched on 4 December 2024.

The information system "shall be established" by the Commission "by 30 December 2024" and contains due diligence statements made available pursuant to Article 4(2). *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 33(1), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115 The Commission confirms: "The Information System as set out in Art. 33 of the Regulation was launched on 4 December 2024. Registration for users of the system was opened on November 2024." *Source: European Commission DG Environment, "Regulation on Deforestation-free Products," European Commission. https://environment.ec.europa.eu/topics/forests/deforestation/regulation-deforestation-free-products_en

*Operational implication:* For workspaces that are downstream operators or non-SME traders, registration in the Information System is required to collect and transmit reference numbers. For operators (first-to-market entities), registration is required to submit or reference due diligence statements.

### 4 — WINDOW CLOSING: Verify supplier geolocation data capability before 30 December 2026

**Action:** Verify whether upstream suppliers (farms, estates, mills, processors) can provide geolocation data in the format the EUDR requires, and identify gaps.

The regulation defines "geolocation" as "the geographical location of a plot of land described by means of latitude and longitude coordinates corresponding to at least one latitude and one longitude point and using at least six decimal digits; for plots of land of more than four hectares used for the production of the relevant commodities other than cattle, this shall be provided using polygons with sufficient latitude and longitude points to describe the perimeter of each plot of land." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 2(28), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

*Operational implication:* For workspaces sourcing from supply chains with many smallholder producers — common in cocoa (West Africa), coffee (Ethiopia, Vietnam), and rubber (Southeast Asia) — securing plot-level polygon data is a supply-chain readiness gap that cannot be resolved at the point of customs declaration.

### 5 — COST ALERT: Penalty exposure up to 4% of total annual Union-wide turnover

**Action:** Brief commercial leadership and legal counsel on penalty exposure now, before any compliance gap assessment is complete.

**Penalty summary slot:** Article 25(2)(a) states that fines shall be "proportionate to the environmental damage and the value of the relevant commodities or relevant products concerned"; "in the case of a legal person, the maximum amount of such a fine shall be at least 4 % of the operator's or trader's total annual Union-wide turnover in the financial year preceding the fining decision." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 25(2)(a), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115 Additional penalties include: confiscation of products, confiscation of revenues, temporary exclusion from public procurement for up to 12 months, temporary prohibition on placing products on the market, and prohibition from exercising simplified due diligence. *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 25(2)(b)–(f), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

### 1 — Information System access and integration

**Scope:** All entities that will submit due diligence statements (operators) or reference numbers (downstream operators and traders) must register in the EUDR Information System.
**Deadline:** Before 30 December 2026 (large/medium operators, downstream operators, traders); before 30 June 2027 (micro/small operators for non-EUTR products; natural persons).
**Gap from current operational baseline:** *Operational implication:* Workspaces without an existing EUDR Information System registration and without an integrated API connection to that system face a registration and IT-integration gap. The Commission plans to relaunch the IS in June 2026 with updated APIs; system integration planning should await the June 2026 API release to avoid rework.

### 2 — Geolocation data collection and management

**Scope:** Operators must collect and maintain geolocation coordinates (minimum 6 decimal places; polygon for plots over 4 hectares for non-cattle commodities) for all plots of land or establishments in their supply chain.
**Deadline:** Before placing any relevant product on the market or exporting from 30 December 2026.
**Gap from current operational baseline:** *Operational implication:* Workspaces whose cargo management systems record country-of-origin data but not plot-level geolocation face a fundamental data gap. Sourcing geolocation from upstream suppliers — particularly smallholders in cocoa, coffee, rubber, and soya supply chains — requires supplier onboarding processes, data collection tools, and verification mechanisms that cannot be built at customs declaration time.

*Operational implication:* The WRI notes that for workspaces sourcing from supply chains with many smallholder producers, "securing plot-level polygon data is a supply-chain readiness gap" that requires engagement well upstream of the EU border. Indonesia, Ghana, and Vietnam are cited as countries investing in government-led geospatial verification systems, which may ease data collection for producers in those origins. *Source: World Resources Institute, "What Is the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR)?", WRI, 15 May 2026. https://www.wri.org/insights/explain-eu-deforestation-regulation

### 3 — Due diligence system documentation and annual review

**Scope:** Non-SME operators must maintain a formal due diligence system framework, review it at least once a year, update it when new developments arise, and keep records of updates for five years.
**Deadline:** System in place before 30 December 2026; annual review thereafter.
**Gap from current operational baseline:** *Operational implication:* Workspaces that have not previously operated a formal commodity due diligence system (separate from customs or trade compliance programs) must build documentation frameworks covering risk assessment criteria, risk mitigation procedures, supplier records, and compliance officer designation.

### 4 — Compliance officer designation (non-SME operators)

Article 11(2)(a) requires "the appointment of a compliance officer at management level for non-SME operators." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 11(2)(a), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115
**Deadline:** Before 30 December 2026.
*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether the workspace qualifies as a non-SME operator (and therefore is subject to this requirement) depends on its defined role under the regulation and its SME status under Directive 2013/34/EU.

### 5 — Customs declaration process modification

**Scope:** The person lodging customs declarations for relevant products entering or leaving the market must include the due diligence statement reference number before the release for free circulation or export.
**Deadline:** 30 December 2026 (when Article 26 applies); the Article 28(1) electronic interface is not expected until 30 June 2028, so manual or system-to-system reference number provision at declaration time is the interim mechanism.
**Gap from current operational baseline:** *Operational implication:* Workspaces acting as customs broker or lodging declarations as importer of record must modify their customs declaration workflows to include the EUDR DDS reference number field. Customs declarations submitted for relevant products without this reference number may result in delays or refusals by customs authorities.

### 6 — Substantiated concern response capability

Article 4(5) states: "Operators that obtain or are made aware of relevant new information, including substantiated concerns, indicating that a relevant product that they have placed on the market is at risk of not complying with this Regulation shall immediately inform the competent authorities of the Member States in which they placed the relevant product on the market, as well as traders to whom they supplied the relevant product." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 4(5), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115
*Operational implication:* Workspaces must establish an internal process for receiving, triaging, and escalating substantiated concerns, including from third parties (NGOs, civil society, other operators), and for notifying competent authorities without undue delay.

### Country-level readiness and traceability systems

Producer countries are developing traceability infrastructure that will affect supply-chain data availability for EUDR compliance. Vietnam has adopted "a national action plan prioritizing sustainable agricultural transformation" and "launched a traceability system for coffee farms, piloting geospatial verification (such as satellite images) in key producing provinces." The system "cross-references land-use maps and registration data to ensure EUDR compliance. Plans are also underway to expand it to rubber and cocoa." *Source: World Resources Institute, "What Is the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR)?", WRI, 15 May 2026. https://www.wri.org/insights/explain-eu-deforestation-regulation

Indonesia, Ghana, and Vietnam are cited as countries "investing in government-led efforts to make information available to companies that must comply with the regulation." *Source: World Resources Institute, "What Is the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR)?", WRI, 15 May 2026. https://www.wri.org/insights/explain-eu-deforestation-regulation

*Analytical inference:* For workspaces sourcing from these origins, government-led traceability programmes may reduce the data collection burden on individual operators by providing publicly accessible geolocation reference datasets. Monitoring these programmes and engaging government contacts in-country is a viable supply-chain strategy.

### EU Observatory on Deforestation and Forest Degradation

The Commission has established an "EU Observatory on deforestation, forest degradation, changes in the world's forest cover and associated drivers" which "should provide for land cover maps, including with time series since the cut-off date defined in this Regulation." The Observatory "should participate in the development of an early warning system combining research and monitoring capacity." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Recital 31, European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115 The Observatory is publicly accessible and provides maps and datasets. *Source: European Commission DG Environment, "Regulation on Deforestation-free Products," European Commission. https://environment.ec.europa.eu/topics/forests/deforestation/regulation-deforestation-free-products_en

*Operational implication:* Workspaces conducting risk assessments (Article 10) can use EU Observatory data as a public, Commission-backed source for identifying deforestation risk in specific production areas, supporting the risk assessment criteria at Article 10(2)(a) and (f).

### Third-party verification and certification schemes

The regulation permits (but does not require) the use of "certification or other third-party verified schemes" in risk assessment, "including voluntary schemes recognised by the Commission under Article 30(5) of Directive (EU) 2018/2001." These may supplement but cannot substitute for operator due diligence responsibility. *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 10(2)(n), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

*Analytical inference:* Certification schemes (e.g., Rainforest Alliance, RSPO for palm oil, FSC/PEFC for timber) provide a partial evidence base for risk assessments but do not satisfy the full geolocation and deforestation-free documentation requirements. Workspaces relying on certification as a primary compliance tool face the risk that certifications do not meet the Article 9 information requirements.

### Team Europe Initiative on Deforestation-free Value Chains

The Commission and EU Member States (Germany, Netherlands, France) have launched a "Team Europe Initiative on Deforestation-free Value Chains … with an initial package of €70 million in funding." *Source: European Commission DG Environment, "Regulation on Deforestation-free Products," European Commission. https://environment.ec.europa.eu/topics/forests/deforestation/regulation-deforestation-free-products_en This initiative supports partner countries in transitioning to sustainable, deforestation-free agricultural value chains.

*Analytical inference:* This initiative may produce technical assistance, traceability tools, and capacity-building resources in producer countries that reduce compliance costs for operators sourcing from those regions over the medium term.

*Operational implication:* The EUDR's Annex I product scope intersects with cargo verticals common to freight and logistics workspaces. Specific exposure depends on the workspace's confirmed transaction types. The following maps Annex I against common freight categories:

**Wood/furniture/paper (common across air freight and general cargo):**
- Furniture (CN 9403 30, 9403 40, 9403 50, 9403 60, 9403 91) — in scope
- Prefabricated wooden buildings (CN 9406 10) — in scope
- Plywood, veneered panels (CN 4412) — in scope
- Pulp and paper (Chapters 47–48) — in scope, exception for bamboo-based and recovered (waste and scrap) products
- Printed books and newspapers (ex 49) — **note: printed products were removed from scope by the December 2025 amendment** per the WRI analysis: "printed products, such as books and publications, [were removed] from the regulation's scope" in December 2025. *Source: World Resources Institute, "What Is the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR)?", WRI, 15 May 2026. https://www.wri.org/insights/explain-eu-deforestation-regulation *Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether ex 49 products remain in the Annex I CN code list as enacted or have been formally removed by an amending implementing act requires verification against the current consolidated Annex I.

**Leather goods (common in luxury/fashion logistics):**
- Raw hides and skins (ex 4101), tanned hides (ex 4104), further-prepared leather (ex 4107) — currently in scope in enacted text
- The draft delegated act (consultation closed 1 June 2026) proposes removal of cattle hides, skins, and leather. *Source: Latham & Watkins / Global ELR, "European Commission Releases New EU Deforestation Regulation Measures," Global ELR, 7 May 2026. https://www.globalelr.com/2026/05/european-commission-releases-new-eu-deforestation-regulation-measures *Operational implication:* Workspaces handling high-value leather goods (handbags, footwear, automotive leather) should monitor delegated act adoption — if leather is removed, EUDR obligations for that vertical fall away.

- New pneumatic tyres (ex 4011) — in scope in enacted text
- Retreaded tyres — draft delegated act proposes removal. *Source: Latham & Watkins / Global ELR, "European Commission Releases New EU Deforestation Regulation Measures," Global ELR, 7 May 2026. https://www.globalelr.com/2026/05/european-commission-releases-new-eu-deforestation-regulation-measures

**Cocoa/coffee/food products (common in perishable and temperature-controlled logistics):**
- Chocolate and cocoa food preparations (CN 1806) — in scope
- Coffee (CN 0901) — in scope; soluble/instant coffee proposed for addition by delegated act
- Palm oil derivatives — partially in scope; additional palm oil derivatives proposed for addition by delegated act

**Cattle/meat (common in refrigerated logistics):**
- Meat of cattle, fresh or chilled (ex 0201); frozen (ex 0202) — in scope
- Prepared/preserved meat (ex 1602 50) — in scope

### Three conditions for all relevant products (Article 3)

The regulation prohibits relevant commodities and relevant products from being placed or made available on the market or exported unless ALL three conditions are satisfied:

"(a) they are deforestation-free; (b) they have been produced in accordance with the relevant legislation of the country of production; and (c) they are covered by a due diligence statement." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 3, European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

### Due diligence system — three-step structure (Article 8)

"Prior to placing relevant products on the market or exporting them, operators shall exercise due diligence with regard to all relevant products supplied by each particular supplier." The due diligence system includes:
- "(a) the collection of information, data and documents needed to fulfil the requirements set out in Article 9;
- (b) risk assessment measures as referred to in Article 10;
- (c) risk mitigation measures as referred to in Article 11." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 8, European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

### Information requirements (Article 9)

Operators must collect, organise, and keep for five years from the date of placing on the market or export:

- Description, trade name, type, and (for wood) "the common name of the species and their full scientific name"
- Quantity (in kilograms net mass and, where applicable, the supplementary unit set out in Annex I to Regulation (EEC) No 2658/87 against the HS code; or, in all other cases, net mass, volume, or number of items)
- Country of production and, where relevant, parts thereof
- "The geolocation of all plots of land where the relevant commodities that the relevant product contains, or has been made using, were produced, as well as the date or time range of production" — qualification: for cattle products, geolocation refers to "all the establishments where the cattle were kept," not individual plot polygons
- For plots of land over four hectares (for commodities other than cattle): polygon geolocation
- Name, postal address, email of suppliers and of downstream operators/traders to whom products are supplied
- "Adequately conclusive and verifiable information that the relevant products are deforestation-free"
- "Adequately conclusive and verifiable information that the relevant commodities have been produced in accordance with the relevant legislation of the country of production, including any arrangement conferring the right to use the respective area for the purposes of the production of the relevant commodity."
*Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 9(1)(a)–(h), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

### "Relevant legislation of the country of production" — defined scope

The regulation defines "relevant legislation of the country of production" as covering: "(a) land use rights; (b) environmental protection; (c) forest-related rules, including forest management and biodiversity conservation, where directly related to wood harvesting; (d) third parties' rights; (e) labour rights; (f) human rights protected under international law; (g) the principle of free, prior and informed consent (FPIC), including as set out in the UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples; (h) tax, anti-corruption, trade and customs regulations." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 2(40), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

### Risk assessment (Article 10) — criteria

Risk assessment considers (among other factors): the country's risk classification under Article 29; presence of forests; presence of indigenous peoples; prevalence of deforestation; source reliability; "concerns in relation to the country of production and origin or parts thereof, such as level of corruption, prevalence of document and data falsification, lack of law enforcement, violations of international human rights, armed conflict or presence of sanctions imposed by the UN Security Council or the Council of the European Union"; complexity of the supply chain; risk of circumvention; and substantiated concerns submitted under Article 31. *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 10(2)(a)–(n), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

Certification or third-party verified schemes "may" be used in risk assessment but "should not substitute the operator's responsibility as regards due diligence." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Recital 52 and Article 10(2)(n), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

### Risk mitigation (Article 11)

Where risk assessment does not reveal no or only negligible risk, operators must "adopt risk mitigation procedures and measures that are adequate to achieve no or only a negligible risk." Mitigation may include: requiring additional information; carrying out independent surveys or audits; "supporting compliance with this Regulation by that operator's suppliers, in particular smallholders, through capacity building and investments." Non-SME operators are specifically required to maintain: "(a) model risk management practices, reporting, record-keeping, internal control and compliance management, including the appointment of a compliance officer at management level; (b) an independent audit function to check the internal policies, controls and procedures." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 11(1)–(2), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

### Due diligence statement (Article 4(2) and Annex II)

Before placing relevant products on the market or exporting them, operators must submit a due diligence statement through the EUDR Information System. The statement must include: operator's name, address, and (for relevant products entering or leaving the market) EORI number; HS code, description, trade name, scientific name (where applicable), and quantity; country of production and geolocation of all plots of land (or establishments for cattle); for downstream references, the reference number of the existing due diligence statement; and a declaration that "due diligence in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2023/1115 was carried out and that no or only a negligible risk was found." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Annex II and Article 4(2), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

"By making available the due diligence statement to competent authorities, the operator shall assume responsibility for the compliance of the relevant product with Article 3." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 4(3), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

### SME operator derogation (Article 4(8))

"Operators that are SMEs ('SME operators') shall not be required to exercise due diligence for relevant products contained in or made from relevant products that have already been subject to due diligence in accordance with paragraph 1 of this Article and for which a due diligence statement has already been submitted in accordance with Article 33. In such cases, SME operators shall provide the competent authorities with the reference number of the due diligence statement upon request. For parts of relevant products that have not been subject to due diligence, the SME operators shall exercise due diligence in accordance with paragraph 1 of this Article." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 4(8), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

### Country benchmarking and simplified due diligence (Articles 13 and 29)

**Three-tier classification:** Countries are classified as "low risk," "standard risk," or "high risk" based on an objective and transparent assessment by the Commission. *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 29(1), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

**Simplified due diligence for low-risk countries (Article 13):** When placing relevant products on the market or exporting them from countries classified as low risk, operators are "not required to fulfil the obligations under Articles 10 and 11" (risk assessment and risk mitigation), after having ascertained that all relevant commodities were produced in low-risk countries and assessed the risk of circumvention. The operator must make available "relevant documentation demonstrating that there is a negligible risk of circumvention of this Regulation or of mixing with products of unknown origin or origin in high-risk or standard-risk countries." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 13(1), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115 The simplification disappears if the operator becomes aware of information pointing to a risk — in that case, full Articles 10 and 11 obligations revive. *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 13(2), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

**Enhanced checks for high-risk countries:** Competent authorities must check "at least 9 % of the operators placing or making available on the market or exporting relevant products that contain or have been made using relevant commodities as well as 9 % of the quantity of each of the relevant products … produced in a country or parts thereof classified as high risk." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 16(9), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

**Standard-risk country check rate:** At least 3% of operators. *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 16(8), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

**Low-risk country check rate:** At least 1% of operators. *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 16(10), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

### Feed for livestock (Recital 39 qualification)

Operators placing cattle-derived products on the market or exporting them must ensure that feed used for livestock does not lead to deforestation: "geolocation requirements under this Regulation should be limited to referring to the geographical location of each of the establishments where the cattle were raised, and no geolocation information should be required for the feed itself." If the competent authority identifies a risk regarding feed, the operator must provide detailed information. "The evidence should cover the lifetime of the animals, up to a maximum of five years." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Recital 39, European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

### Penalties (Article 25) — full time series

The regulation does not set out a penalty trajectory that changes by date. The penalty provisions apply from the date of application. Penalties include:
- Fines of at least 4% of total annual Union-wide turnover for legal persons (maximum amount, not the minimum — fines must be proportionate and must "effectively deprive those responsible of the economic benefits derived from their infringements")
- Confiscation of products and revenues
- Temporary exclusion from public procurement for up to 12 months
- Temporary prohibition from placing relevant products on the market
- Prohibition from exercising simplified due diligence (for serious or repeated infringements)
*Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 25(2), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115
